# BPCS Interlock Specification Template and Example

## Rules for using the template

1. **Setpoints, delays, deadbands and tolerances appear only in Section 3 (Parameter Register).** Everywhere else, including logic text, alarm tables and FAT steps, refer to them by parameter ID (e.g. `P-01`). If you find a number outside Section 3, it is a defect.
2. **One interlock = one record = one ID.** Cause-and-effect matrices, FAT sheets and configuration reports should be generated from or checked against these records, not retyped.
3. **Section 3 maps to a named DCS location** (tag.parameter) so the configurer enters each value once and FAT reads it from the system.
4. **BPCS only.** If anything here is credited as an independent protection layer in a LOPA, or overlaps an SIF, stop and route it to the SRS.

---

## Template

### 0. Header
| Field | Entry |
|---|---|
| Interlock ID | `<UNIT>-IL-<nnn>` |
| Title | |
| Unit / Area | |
| Revision / Date / Status | Draft / Reviewed / Approved / Implemented / FAT'd |
| Classification | BPCS process interlock. Confirm: not an SIF, not a LOPA-credited layer |
| Legacy source(s) | Printout no./page, C&E drawing no./row/column, as-found values |
| New DCS location | Controller / module / function block name |

### 1. Purpose and Hazard
One or two sentences on what this prevents and the consequence if it fails to act.

### 2. Causes (Inputs)
| Ref | Tag | Description | Signal type / range / units | Voting | Bad-quality / out-of-range action |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

### 3. Parameter Register (single source of truth)
| ID | Description | Value | Units | Applies to (tag) | DCS parameter location | Basis / origin | Change authority |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

Include trip and alarm setpoints, deadbands, on/off delays, reset thresholds, timers and test tolerance.

### 4. Logic Description
- **4.1 Trip condition** (written using Ref and parameter IDs)
- **4.2 Delays / filtering**
- **4.3 Latching and reset conditions**
- **4.4 Permissives / conditions for restart**
- **4.5 Modes** (e.g. start-up override, maintenance bypass: when allowed, by whom, how indicated)
- **4.6 Logic sketch or truth table** (optional)

### 5. Effects (Outputs)
| Ref | Tag | Action on trip | De-energized / fail state | Feedback / confirmation | Other effects (alarms, other interlocks, controller mode changes) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

### 6. Alarms and Annunciation
| Tag/Message | Condition (parameter IDs) | Priority | Operator action |
|---|---|---|---|

### 7. Fault Handling
Behavior on loss of signal, bad quality, communications loss, controller failover and power restoration.

### 8. Configuration Notes
Block types, scan class, execution order, and anything the configurer must not "improve."

### 9. FAT Test Steps
| Step | Precondition | Action | Expected result | Parameter refs | Pass/Fail | Initials |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

Test values are expressed relative to parameters (e.g. "P-01 minus P-05"). The actual value is read from the register at test time.

### 10. Open Items and Legacy Discrepancies
| # | Legacy vs. new difference or question | Owner | Resolution |
|---|---|---|---|

### 11. Approvals
Process / Operations / Control Systems / Safety (confirming BPCS classification) / FAT lead.

---

## Filled-in Example

*All numbers below are illustrative placeholders. Replace them with values from your legacy documentation and process safety basis.*

### 0. Header
| Field | Entry |
|---|---|
| Interlock ID | `U11-IL-004` |
| Title | Heater H-1101 low fuel gas pressure: close main fuel valve |
| Unit / Area | Unit 11, Crude Heater |
| Revision / Status | Rev A / Draft |
| Classification | BPCS process interlock. Not an SIF; not credited in LOPA (confirm with safety, see Open Item 2) |
| Legacy source(s) | Logic printout `<no./page>`; C&E drawing `<no.>`, row `<n>` |
| New DCS location | `<Controller>/<Module>/U11_IL_004` |

### 1. Purpose and Hazard
Prevents burner flameout and unstable combustion caused by low fuel gas header pressure. Loss of flame with continued fuel admission risks a firebox accumulation and re-light explosion.

### 2. Causes
| Ref | Tag | Description | Signal / range / units | Voting | Bad quality action |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | PT-1105 | Fuel gas pressure at heater battery limit | 4–20 mA, 0–600 kPag | 1oo1 | Treat as trip condition (fail to safe) after P-04 |

### 3. Parameter Register
| ID | Description | Value | Units | Applies to | DCS parameter | Basis | Change authority |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| P-01 | Low-low trip setpoint | 140 | kPag | PT-1105 | `U11_IL_004.TRIP_SP` | Legacy printout; min. stable burner pressure | Process Eng. + MOC |
| P-02 | Low alarm setpoint | 200 | kPag | PT-1105 | `PT1105.PVLO_LIM` | Legacy alarm list | Process Eng. |
| P-03 | Reset threshold | 170 | kPag | PT-1105 | `U11_IL_004.RESET_SP` | Gives margin above P-01 (30 kPag) | Process Eng. + MOC |
| P-04 | Trip on-delay (and bad-quality delay) | 2 | s | U11_IL_004 | `U11_IL_004.TRIP_DLY` | Legacy timer; rejects transients | Process Eng. + MOC |
| P-05 | FAT test tolerance on trip point | ±2 | kPag | FAT | n/a (test only) | Transmitter + simulator accuracy | FAT lead |

### 4. Logic Description
- **4.1 Trip:** C1 value < P-01 continuously for P-04, **or** C1 quality bad for P-04.
- **4.2 Delay:** On-delay P-04 applies to both conditions. There is no off-delay.
- **4.3 Latch / reset:** Trip latches. Reset requires all of: C1 > P-03, C1 quality good, and operator reset command from the faceplate. There is no auto-reset.
- **4.4 Restart permissive:** Latch must be cleared before XV-1106 can be commanded open. Opening remains a manual operator action.
- **4.5 Modes:** No bypass is provided for this interlock. The start-up override in the legacy logic is *not* carried forward (see Open Item 1).
- **4.6 Truth table:**

| Latch | C1 vs. thresholds | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Clear | C1 ≥ P-01, good | XV-1106 may be open |
| Clear | C1 < P-01 for P-04, or bad for P-04 | Set latch; close XV-1106 |
| Set | C1 > P-03, good, reset commanded | Clear latch |
| Set | otherwise | Remain tripped |

### 5. Effects
| Ref | Tag | Action on trip | Fail state | Feedback | Other effects |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | XV-1106 | De-energize solenoid; close main fuel gas valve | Energize to open, spring closes | ZSC/ZSO-1106; alarm if not closed within `<valve stroke time>` | Pilot gas not affected. Heater temperature controller output set to track/manual |

### 6. Alarms
| Message | Condition | Priority | Operator action |
|---|---|---|---|
| PAL-1105 Fuel gas pressure low | C1 < P-02 | Medium | Check fuel gas header, supply pressure controller |
| U11-IL-004 TRIPPED | Latch set | High | Verify cause, follow heater trip procedure; reset only after C1 > P-03 |
| XV-1106 fails to close | E1 commanded closed, no ZSC after stroke time | High | Local isolation per procedure |

### 7. Fault Handling
- **Loss of C1 signal or bad quality:** trips after P-04.
- **Controller failover:** latch state must be retained through failover. Verify in FAT.
- **Power restoration:** latch initializes **set** (tripped) after a controller cold start; the valve stays closed.

### 8. Configuration Notes
- Use the standard latch block with reset priority. Do not combine with the PAL alarm block.
- Alarm and trip use the same PV tag, but each reads its own parameter (P-02 vs. P-01). Do not derive one from the other.
- Write the output to XV-1106 from this interlock only. The valve's regular control module must have this interlock as its highest-priority override.

### 9. FAT Test Steps
| Step | Precondition | Action | Expected | Params | P/F | Init. |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | XV-1106 open, latch clear, PT-1105 simulated normal | Ramp C1 down slowly | PAL-1105 annunciates when C1 crosses P-02 | P-02, P-05 | | |
| 2 | As above | Continue ramp down through P-01 | After P-04, trip alarm active, XV-1106 de-energized and closed, controller output tracking. Record actual trip value; must be within P-05 of P-01 | P-01, P-04, P-05 | | |
| 3 | Step 2 complete | Drop C1 to below P-01 for less than P-04, then restore (from a latch-clear, valve-open state) | No trip | P-01, P-04 | | |
| 4 | Latch set | Raise C1 above P-01 but below P-03; press reset | Reset rejected, latch remains set | P-01, P-03 | | |
| 5 | Latch set | Raise C1 above P-03; press reset | Latch clears, valve stays closed until operator opens it | P-03 | | |
| 6 | Latch clear, C1 normal | Force C1 bad quality (disconnect simulated signal) | After P-04, trip as in step 2 | P-04 | | |
| 7 | Latch set | Force controller failover | Latch remains set, valve remains closed | n/a | | |
| 8 | Latch clear, valve open | Attempt to open XV-1106 from graphic while latch is set (repeat of step 2 state) | Command is blocked | n/a | | |

### 10. Open Items
| # | Item | Owner | Resolution |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Legacy logic has a start-up override of this trip. Confirm whether it is required, and if so, define it as a separate controlled bypass with timeout | Operations / Process | Open |
| 2 | Confirm with safety team that this is not a credited layer in the heater LOPA | Safety | Open |
| 3 | Confirm P-01 and P-04 against the legacy printout and the burner manufacturer minimum | Process Eng. | Open |

### 11. Approvals
Process ____  Operations ____  Control Systems ____  Safety ____  FAT lead ____

---

## Practical suggestions for 40 units

- **Keep the parameter register as a table or spreadsheet export** that generates Section 3 for each record, so the configurer and the FAT team both read from the same row. A change to P-01 then happens in one place.
- **Do a reconciliation pass.** For each interlock, record the legacy value and the new value side by side, and treat any difference as an Open Item that needs a decision rather than a silent change.
- **Use consistent parameter IDs** (`P-nn` per record) and consistent DCS parameter naming so scripts can compare the register against the live configuration after loading.
- **Standardize the common patterns** (low/high trip with latch, 2oo3 transmitter, permissive-to-start) as sub-templates, since most of the 40 units will repeat them.

I can also draft a 2oo3 variant or a spreadsheet column layout for the parameter register if that is useful.
